nodes.label:
Wait between pressing modifiers (Shift, Ctrl, …) and the main key of a macro step. Increase it if an application receives the shortcut without its modifier. Default for macros that leave the field empty.

Standard value: 5 ms.

Pause between consecutive steps of a macro. Increase it if an application misses keystrokes.

Standard value: 20 ms.

How long to keep holding a rule key before its long-hold action runs once. Applies to rules whose hold runs an action instead of a layer.

Standard value: 1000 ms.

How long to hold a rule key before it counts as a hold: its layer or hold action. Released earlier, the key runs its tap action.

Lower: layers turn on faster, but fast typing may trigger them by mistake. Higher: fewer false holds, but a longer wait. Usually 150–250 ms.

Standard value: 200 ms.

nodes.value: After another key is released (better for typing)

nodes.label:
Decides when a dual-role key counts as a hold if another key is pressed. Rules can override this default in advanced options. Chord detection is configured separately.

After another key is released: the key becomes a hold once another key is pressed and released while it is down, or when the hold threshold passes. Fast rolls while typing stay taps.

As soon as another key is pressed: useful for dedicated layer or modifier keys. Reacts faster, but overlapping letters while typing can trigger the hold by mistake.

A second tap within this time after the first release counts as a double tap.

A single tap on a key with a double-tap action runs only after this window ends, so a large value makes such keys feel slow. Keys without a double-tap action are not delayed.

Standard value: 200 ms.

A macro still running after this time is stopped and counts as finished. A macro started while another one runs waits for it; up to 3 runs can wait, further presses are ignored.

Standard value: 10000 ms.

For rules triggered by several keys pressed together, such as KeyJ+KeyK. All keys must go down within this time, in any order. Until then the first key is held back; if the combination does not complete, it is typed as usual. Modifiers are never held back.

Higher: the combination is easier to hit, but typing with these keys lags slightly. Applies to all rules; a rule cannot override it.

Standard value: 50 ms.
